pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.49 a.1
pairs.question: Utrum bonum possit esse causa mali?
pairs.answer: Necesse est dicere quod omne malum aliqualiter causam habeat.
pairs.derivation: Question is the article title 'Utrum bonum possit esse causa mali', stripping the 'ARTICULUS 1' scaffolding header; normalized terminal punctuation to '?'. Answer: dropped the framing 'Respondeo dicendum quod' (Aquinas's 'I answer that' tag) at the start of the Respondeo; took the first operative answering sentence, which affirms that all evil does have a cause (the article's thesis, developed below as cause per accidens). Cut before 'Malum enim est defectus boni...' which begins the supporting elaboration.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.49 a.2
pairs.question: Utrum summum bonum, quod est Deus, sit causa mali?
pairs.answer: Malum quod in defectu actionis consistit, vel quod ex defectu agentis causatur, non reducitur in Deum sicut in causam.
pairs.derivation: Question is the article title 'Utrum summum bonum, quod est Deus, sit causa mali', stripping the 'ARTICULUS 2' header; normalized terminal punctuation to '?'. Answer: skipped the non-answering preamble 'Respondeo dicendum quod, sicut ex dictis patet, malum quod in defectu actionis consistit, semper causatur ex defectu agentis. In Deo autem nullus defectus est, sed summa perfectio, ut supra ostensum est.' (recapitulation of prior results, not the answer), and advanced the start to the 'Unde...'-introduced operative conclusion; dropped the leading connective 'Unde' so the answer begins on a verbatim contiguous span. pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.49 a.3
pairs.question: Utrum sit unum summum malum, quod sit causa omnis mali?
pairs.answer: Ex praedictis patet non esse unum primum principium malorum, sicut est unum primum principium bonorum.

Answer: dropped the framing 'Respondeo dicendum quod' and took the first operative answering sentence, which directly denies a single first principle of evils.
